set.name: Southeast Route
set.best_season: Best from mid-July through October, when the brush is dry and snow is off the crest. Snow in November to May makes the talus and crest slow and avalanche-prone on the talus slope, though the road walk stays open for foot or bike travel.
set.approach: Walk or bike the closed continuation of the Middle Fork road east from the Dingford Creek trailhead for about 4 miles, to the short side road to the hot-springs parking area at roughly 1,800 ft. Leave the road there and head north, bending north-northwest onto the north-south spur ridge that rises from it.
set.beta: Follow the spur through forest to about 4,400 ft, where the trees give way to an open talus slope. Climb the talus, or its edge, to the east-west crest near 5,100 ft, then turn west along the crest, staying on its forested north side because the south face is cliffy. Expect rock steps and towers to be passed or skirted, with hands needed in places. Route-finding is the main challenge. About 3,700 ft of gain and 2 to 3 miles off-trail beyond the road walk, which adds about 8 miles round trip; allow 3 to 5 hours up from the spur. The line stays outside the Alpine Lakes Wilderness.
hazards: Exposed crest with loose rock steps, and cliffs on its south side
The long road walk makes a descent in the dark likely
Snow-loaded talus in winter and spring
